newsitem.title: POLAND: RWE eyes major investments in Polish power.
newsitem.headline: RWE eyes major investments in Polish power.

text.p: German energy group RWE AG could invest up to three billion marks ($1.7 billion) in Poland's electricity industry in the long term if conditions are right, a senior RWE official said on Tuesday.

Klaus Bussfeld, board member of the group's electricity unit RWE Energie AG, told a news conference in the western city of Poznan that the firm might consider putting money into two major power plants in Poland.

"Our cooperation is aimed at long-term activities but if conditions arise that would make this possible, we would be able to invest up to one billion marks in Laziska and two billion in Belchatow," he said.
Bussfeld said RWE wanted to boost its Polish presence by signing cooperation deals with local firms and possibly by investing in the expansion of Poland's energy sector.
He said RWE Energie had on Tuesday signed a cooperation agreement with Poland's largest state-owned power plant, Belchatow, its fifth such deal with a Polish electricity firm.
It was preparing another agreement with the Krakow electricity company, he added.

Bussfeld, speaking during a two-day energy conference in Poznan, said RWE saw Poland's electricity market, the largest in Central Europe and set for high growth, as very attractive especially in the long-term.

He said RWE had already signed an agreement with Laziska in southern Poland to develop its new 500-megawatt coal-powered unit and would bid in a tender to build a $1 billion, 800-megawatt lignite plant in Belchatow near the central city of Lodz.
"We plan to bid in the tender and we believe we have strong chances because we are a leading world player in lignite power generation technology," Bussfeld said.

He said RWE might seek the role of strategic investor in the new plant, due for completion in 2003, but was also ready for partnerships with Polish companies in which it would have minority interests.
"We would like to be a strategic partner but we are also open for partnerships with local companies in Poland with RWE participation," he said.
